opening.headline: To split AI cost invoices that arrive at the end of the month by department, what criteria and data are required?
body: AI billing statements typically arrive as a single total for the entire organization. The finance team wants to know departmental cost allocations, but each department does not know its own usage. When multiple teams share a single shared gateway, the provider records only one set of credentials. Without knowing the cause of cost increases, it is impossible to identify the source, and without identifying the source, control is unattainable.

In this class, we first verify the data provided by the usage and cost APIs. Next, we examine how to assign workspaces and projects as cost centers, as well as allocation strategies, tagging, and shared cost distribution as discussed in the FinOps allocation concept. Finally, we walk through a case study of allocating shared gateway costs proportionally based on usage.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the concepts of capacity and cost APIs and FinOps allocation.
Workspace and project-level assignment methods can be distinguished.

screens.title: An invoice line cannot be split by department.
screens.lead: First, review the invoice that shows only the total across the organization. The diagram illustrates how usage from three departments is mixed behind a single authentication.

visual.alt: A diagram showing three departments going to the supplier through a single shared gateway, resulting in the supplier invoice having only one total.
labels: What is the departmental cost share?

paragraphs: AI cost invoices arrive at the end of the month. The figure is a single total for the entire organization. The finance team wants to know how much each department should bear. However, each department does not know how much it has actually used.

If multiple teams call models through a single shared gateway, the problem becomes more severe. For example, the Claude Apps Gateway inherently forwards all inference requests through a single top-level credential, causing provider invoices to attribute all usage to that one credential rather than to individual developers. Invoice data alone does not reveal which department spent how much.
Without a cost assignment basis, it is impossible to identify the cause when costs increase, and since no department can be held accountable, there is no way to control costs.

callout.label: Questions to be answered in this class
callout.text: To whom shall usage be allocated, and how shall costs shared among multiple departments be distributed?

screens.outro: First, let's recall the current standards of our organization.

screens.title: Think about the criteria for allocating costs by department
screens.lead: First, think through each question on your own before selecting an answer. The instructor's thoughts will then be organized and presented. No answers are submitted.

items.prompt: If departments are divided by API key, isn't it possible that multiple teams are sharing the same key?
items.answer: If one key is shared among multiple teams, dividing the key by team will not result in distinct team identification. For a key to represent a department, there must be a one-to-one correspondence between the key and the department.

items.prompt: Are you already using a unit such as a project or workspace to bundle usage?
items.answer: Providers typically offer units that bundle usage. Claude provides workspaces, while Gemini applies limits on a project basis. By aligning these units with departments or services, usage is automatically segmented without requiring additional setup.

items.prompt: Are you indicating usage with metadata such as tags or labels?
items.answer: Tags are a supplementary means used when account or project structure alone is insufficient. Without rules defining which tags to use, omissions and typos will accumulate, so rules and validation must be provided together.

items.prompt: Should costs shared among multiple departments, such as gateway or support fees, be borne by whom?
items.answer: The answer is not unique. There are several methods: dividing by departmental usage, distributing equally, or allocating based on central budget. Regardless of the method chosen, it is important first to establish a baseline.

screens.outro: Since the required data varies depending on the standard, let's first examine where usage data is obtained.

screens.title: What the Usage and Cost API reveals
screens.lead: The following are three requests to call Claude's Usage and Cost Admin API. Check, alongside the right-side explanations, how these can be grouped and filtered by unit.

data.code:
#1) Retrieves daily usage volumes by model, for the most recent month.
curl "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/usage_report/messages?\
starting_at=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z&\
ending_at=2025-01-31T00:00:00Z&\
group_by%5B%5D=model&\
bucket_width=1d" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY"

#2) Filter to view only the usage of a specific workspace.
curl "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/usage_report/messages?\
starting_at=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z&\
ending_at=2025-01-08T00:00:00Z&\
workspace_ids%5B%5D=wrkspc_01JwQvzr7rXLA5AGx3HKfFUJ&\
bucket_width=1d" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY"

#3) Retrieve costs grouped by workspace and explanation unit.
curl "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/cost_report?\
starting_at=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z&\
ending_at=2025-01-31T00:00:00Z&\
group_by%5B%5D=workspace_id&\
group_by%5B%5D=description" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY"

notes.note: Daily usage is grouped by model. This API retrieves an organization's historical usage programmatically, and requires an Admin API key rather than a general key. An authentication error occurs if the key type is incorrect. The square brackets for repeatable parameters are encoded in URL format as `%5B%5D`.

Filter by workspace ID to view usage data for a specific department or service. You can also filter or group by API key, workspace, model, service tier, and other criteria. The available query intervals are 1 minute, 1 hour, or 1 day.

This is a cost report. Costs are based on USD and can be grouped by workspace or by unit of description, or provided on a per-day basis. It also separately displays costs for web searches and code execution, in addition to token usage.

This data can be used for reconciliation between invoices and internal records. However, Claude Enterprise (claude.ai) organizations must use a different API than the Admin API key, so organizations must first verify which product they are using.

screens.outro: Having verified the methods for obtaining data, we will now examine the unit responsible for attributing usage to specific parties.

screens.title: Workspace and project-specific allocation method
screens.lead: When you select the image number marker, you can view detailed descriptions by assigned unit.

visual.alt: Under a single organization, multiple workspaces exist, each bound to a key and a limit, and the shared gateway is structured with a separate path.

markers.label: Organization and Default Workspace
markers.title: A basic workspace available to all organizations
markers.body: Claude organization always has a Default Workspace that cannot be renamed or deleted. Additional workspaces can be created to separate projects, environments, and teams, with billing and management handled centrally. The organization-wide default limit is 100. The usage of a Default Workspace appears in reports as `workspace_id` to `null`.

markers.label: Limit the key to the workspace
markers.title: The API key becomes a unit of departmental ownership.
markers.body: If an API key is restricted to a specific workspace, the key can only access resources within that workspace. By assigning a workspace to each department and allowing the key within that workspace to be used, the key's usage directly corresponds to the department's usage. Workspace IDs begin with `wrkspc_`.

markers.label: Claude Code Workspace
markers.title: The only workspace that supports per-user limits
markers.body: When you first log in with Claude Code, an organization-level Claude Code workspace is automatically created. This workspace is the only one that supports per-user monthly spending limits and separates Claude Code traffic from other API workloads.

markers.label: Shared Gateway
markers.title: Structure appearing with a single authentication credential
markers.body: With a shared gateway, the provider invoice shows only one credential. The gateway allows setting spending limits per user on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis, and Amazon Bedrock also offers a developer-level cost allocation feature. The limit amounts are cost estimates and therefore must align with the provider's usage reporting for reconciliation.

markers.label: Tenant-specific measurement
markers.title: The service does not automatically divide it.
markers.body: In multi-tenant environments, most services do not automatically differentiate usage by tenant. Therefore, you must define what constitutes a tenant and directly design the measurement methodology. Gemini applies limits at the project level, making it natural to treat projects as the allocation unit.

screens.outro: Once a cost ownership unit is defined, a framework is needed to link this data to the organization's cost management approach. We'll examine FinOps allocation.

screens.title: FinOps allocation: strategy, tagging, shared costs
screens.lead: The following flashcard describes four activities of FinOps allocation. Select the card to flip it. Use the right arrow to advance to the next card.

cards.front: What is cost allocation in FinOps?
cards.back: Define a strategy using accounts, tags, labels, and metadata to allocate and share costs and usage across teams and projects within an organization, linking invoice line items to cost owners.

Define the organizational units to which costs will be allocated. Define a group of organizations responsible for assigning all costs, and also define a term to refer to each group. In the example from this course, the sales, development, and support departments are the organizational units.

Define tags, labels, naming conventions, and grouping structures to indicate which cost bundle a resource belongs to. Structure the components that can be divided into workspaces or projects, and represent the rest using tags.

Determine which costs to consider as shared costs and how to allocate them. Gateway operation expenses or support fees fall under this category. Costs can be allocated based on usage proportions or equally distributed, or alternatively, they can be retained under a central budget without separate allocation.
A device is provided to verify that allocations are complete. Periodically check for missing tags or unknown departmental usage, and the goal is to reduce the unallocated ratio.

screens.outro: Since the template has been organized, let's apply it to the scenario of sharing gateway costs.

screens.title: Explanation: The shared gateway cost is allocated proportionally based on usage.
screens.lead: The instructor breaks down the scenario step by step. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Verify the example
steps.body: Sales, development, and support departments call models through a single gateway. The supplier invoice shows only one authentication usage, while shared costs such as gateway operations and support fees are billed separately each month.

steps.title: A department identifier is retained for each request.
steps.body: The gateway records a department identifier for each request and verifies that the total matches the supplier's usage data. The gateway's budget limit is an estimate, so settlement is based on the supplier's data.

steps.title: Direct costs are assigned directly.
steps.body: The model usage fees charged per department are directly attributed to that department based on either workspace or key criteria. There is no need to allocate or split this portion.

steps.title: Shared costs are divided by token usage ratio.
steps.body: Gateway operating costs and support fees are allocated based on each department's token usage ratio. For example, if a department uses 40% of the total tokens, it bears 40% of the shared costs. Since costs are incurred proportionally to usage, responsibilities and burdens align.

steps.title: Check for unallocated capacity
steps.body: Unidentified usage is retained as unallocated, and its ratio is periodically reviewed to reduce omissions. As unallocated usage increases, the reliability of proportional allocation decreases, making this review equivalent to allocation compliance verification. If the ratio remains high, it is necessary to investigate whether any call paths omit identifiers.

steps.title: Report by month
steps.body: It enables each department to review monthly results and verify their share and supporting rationale. When the rationale is clear, departments can change their usage habits, leading to cost control. The report should include direct costs, allocated shared costs, and unallocated cost percentages.

screens.outro: Next, we will compare how the burden on departments changes when the allocation method is different.

screens.title: Explanation: Departmental burden varies depending on the allocation method.
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare the three methods for sharing costs, each with its own characteristics. None of these methods is always correct.

tabs.label: Even distribution
tabs.body: Divide shared costs equally among departments. The calculation is simple and easy to explain. However, this creates an unfair situation where departments using fewer resources bear a larger share. For example, if the monthly shared cost is 3 million won and there are three departments, each department bears 1 million won regardless of actual usage. This approach is acceptable when usage differences are small and costs are low.

tabs.label: Usage proportional
tabs.body: Divide the token usage rate by department. This aligns usage responsibility with burden, making it easier for departments to understand and accept. Instead, rules are needed to specify how unidentified usage by departments should be handled. A system must be in place to record the department for each request, and compliance verification must also be conducted to monitor unallocated rates.

tabs.label: Central burden
tabs.body: We do not allocate shared costs to departments from the central budget. This is akin to the "ignore and move on" choice discussed in FinOps. Costs are reduced in terms of calculation and reporting. However, departments cease to be aware of costs, weakening their motivation to reduce usage. This approach is suitable when shared costs are small and not worth dividing.

tabs.label: Selection criteria
tabs.body: No single approach is the only correct solution. Instead, evaluate approaches based on the scale of shared costs, the accuracy of department identification, and the intent to change departmental behavior, and select the one that provides the greatest value. Regardless of the chosen approach, rules must be documented, and impacts on departments must be recorded whenever rules are modified.

screens.outro: Now I will summarize everything discussed so far into a single reference point.

screens.title: Summary: Without an allocation basis, there is no cost accounting.
screens.lead: Summarize the content discussed so far. Please read the following paragraphs in sequence.

paragraphs: To control costs, you must first determine which entity the costs are allocated to. Use the usage and cost APIs to obtain usage and cost data at the model, workspace, and key levels, and allocate costs at the workspace and project level as the base units. When API keys are restricted to a workspace, the usage of the key directly becomes the department's usage.

Places structurally similar to shared gateways, where usage can mix, retain a department identifier for each request to provide compensation. In multi-tenant environments, services do not automatically distribute usage, so measurement methods must be designed directly.

FinOps allocation consists of allocation strategy, tagging and hierarchy strategy, shared cost allocation strategy, and allocation compliance validation. Shared costs are divided based on the size of the costs and the accuracy of identification, and these rules must be documented. Only then can departments understand the results and repeat the process in the following month.

glossary.def: An administrator-only API that groups and queries organizational usage and costs by model, workspace, API key, and other parameters. An Admin API key is required for calls.
It is a unit that divides usage by project, team, or environment within an organization, with separate keys and limits, and billing and management handled centrally.
Activity of assigning costs to cost centers using accounts, tags, labels, and metadata, and sharing cost allocations.
It involves dividing shared costs across departments according to rules such as usage proportion.

misconceptions.myth: You can know the departmental costs if there is an invoice.
misconceptions.fact: If the invoice contains only a total amount and no allocation information, it cannot be distributed by department. In particular, shared gateways display usage aggregated under a single authentication.

misconceptions.myth: Shared costs are most fair when evenly distributed.
misconceptions.fact: Equal distribution may result in unfairness where departments using less bear a greater burden. It should be compared with usage-based or central burden models, evaluated based on cost magnitude and identification accuracy.

misconceptions.myth: An API key alone is sufficient.
misconceptions.fact: The key range, workspace, and tag rules must be present together. And compliance validation to ensure no omissions in assignment is required to reduce unused capacity.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: If there is no ownership criterion, there is also no cost allocation.
Use and Cost API to obtain usage and costs by model, workspace, and key.
Workspaces and projects are the fundamental units of ownership, and the key range supports them.
FinOps allocation is composed of strategy, tagging, shared cost allocation, and compliance validation.

checks.explain: With a shared gateway, only one credential is recorded on the provider's side. Therefore, the gateway retains a department identifier and matches it against usage data or uses a user-level attribution feature.

wrong.0: The supplier does not automatically partition departments behind the gateway since it does not know who they are.
wrong.2: Equal distribution may result in unfairness where departments using less resources bear a greater burden, and billing alone is insufficient to provide call-unit information.
wrong.3: Because it uses a single identity proof, user differentiation does not occur automatically.
